    CREATE OBJECT mo_container
      EXPORTING
        container_name = 'CUSTOM_CONTAINER'.

    CREATE OBJECT mo_tree
      EXPORTING
        parent = mo_container.

    " Register event handler
    SET HANDLER handle_node_double_click FOR mo_tree.

    ls_column-id = 'CARRID'. ls_column-caption = 'Airline'. ls_column-width = 15. APPEND ls_column TO lt_column_table.
    ls_column-id = 'CONNID'. ls_column-caption = 'Connection'. ls_column-width = 10. APPEND ls_column TO lt_column_table.
    ls_column-id = 'FLDATE'. ls_column-caption = 'Flight Date'. ls_column-width = 12. APPEND ls_column TO lt_column_table.

    CALL METHOD mo_tree->set_table_for_first_display
      EXPORTING
        i_structure_name = 'SFLIGHT'
        it_column_list   = lt_column_table.

    SELECT carrid, connid, fldate FROM sflight INTO TABLE @lt_sflight UP TO 10 ROWS.

    LOOP AT lt_sflight INTO DATA(ls_flight).
      ls_node_data-node_key = ls_flight-carrid && ls_flight-connid && ls_flight-fldate.
      ls_node_data-carrid = ls_flight-carrid.
      ls_node_data-connid = ls_flight-connid.
      ls_node_data-fldate = ls_flight-fldate.
      APPEND ls_node_data TO lt_node_data.
    ENDLOOP.

    CALL METHOD mo_tree->add_nodes
      EXPORTING
        i_relative_node_key = cl_gui_column_tree=>root_node
        i_position          = cl_gui_column_tree=>node_position_last
        it_table_structure  = 'TY_NODE_DATA'
        it_table            = lt_node_data.

    CALL METHOD mo_tree->frontend_update.
    CALL METHOD cl_gui_cfw=>flush.

  ENDMETHOD.

  METHOD handle_node_double_click.
    MESSAGE i000(00) WITH 'Node double-clicked:' node_key.
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.

Instructions: Ermitteln Sie zur Laufzeit den Namen der Klasse, auf die eine Objekt-Referenz zeigt, und geben Sie diesen aus.
hint: Verwenden Sie `CL_ABAP_OBJECTDESCR=>GET_P_OBJECT_TYPE` und `GET_NAME`.
solution:
CLASS zcl_rtti_object_type DEFINITION PUBLIC FINAL CREATE PUBLIC.
  PUBLIC SECTION.
    METHODS get_object_class_name IMPORTING io_object TYPE REF TO object
                                  RETURNING VALUE(rv_class_name) TYPE string.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_rtti_object_type IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD get_object_class_name.
    DATA: lr_obj_descr TYPE REF TO cl_abap_objectdescr.

    IF io_object IS BOUND.
      lr_obj_descr ?= cl_abap_typedescr=>describe_by_object_ref( io_object ).
      rv_class_name = lr_obj_descr->get_name( ).
    ELSE.
      rv_class_name = 'Initial Object Reference'.
    ENDIF.
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.
unit_test:
CLASS ltcl_test DEFINITION FOR TESTING RISK LEVEL HARMLESS DURATION SHORT.
  PRIVATE SECTION.
    METHODS test_get_class_name FOR TESTING.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS ltcl_test IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD test_get_class_name.
    DATA(lo_cut) = NEW zcl_rtti_object_type( ).
    DATA(lo_test_object) = NEW zcl_rtti_object_type( ).

    DATA(lv_class_name) = lo_cut->get_object_class_name( lo_test_object ).
    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_equals( act = lv_class_name exp = 'ZCL_RTTI_OBJECT_TYPE' ).

    DATA: lr_initial_object TYPE REF TO object.
    lv_class_name = lo_cut->get_object_class_name( lr_initial_object ).
    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_equals( act = lv_class_name exp = 'Initial Object Reference' ).
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.
explanation: Dieses Beispiel demonstriert die Verwendung von RTTI (Run-Time Type Information) mit Objekt-Referenzen. Mittels `cl_abap_typedescr=>describe_by_object_ref` kann der Typ eines Objekts zur Laufzeit ermittelt und dessen Klassenname über `get_name()` abgerufen werden. Dies ist nützlich für generische Verarbeitungen oder Debugging.
keywords: REF TO, RTTI, CL_ABAP_TYPEDESCR, CL_ABAP_OBJECTDESCR, Object Orientation

Instructions: Implementieren Sie eine Klasse, deren Methoden verkettet aufgerufen werden können (Method Chaining), um eine Konfiguration schrittweise aufzubauen.
hint: Jede Methode, die verkettet werden soll, muss `RETURNING VALUE(result) TYPE REF TO <class_name>` deklarieren und `result = ME` zurückgeben.
solution:
CLASS zcl_config_builder DEFINITION PUBLIC FINAL CREATE PUBLIC.
  PUBLIC SECTION.
    DATA: mv_setting1 TYPE string READ-ONLY,
          mv_setting2 TYPE string READ-ONLY.

    METHODS set_setting1 IMPORTING iv_value TYPE string
                           RETURNING VALUE(ro_me) TYPE REF TO zcl_config_builder.
    METHODS set_setting2 IMPORTING iv_value TYPE string
                           RETURNING VALUE(ro_me) TYPE REF TO zcl_config_builder.
    METHODS build RETURNING VALUE(rs_config) TYPE REF TO zcl_config_builder.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_config_builder IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD set_setting1.
    mv_setting1 = iv_value.
    ro_me = me.
  ENDMETHOD.

  METHOD set_setting2.
    mv_setting2 = iv_value.
    ro_me = me.
  ENDMETHOD.

  METHOD build.
    ro_me = me.
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.
unit_test:
CLASS ltcl_test DEFINITION FOR TESTING RISK LEVEL HARMLESS DURATION SHORT.
  PRIVATE SECTION.
    METHODS test_method_chaining FOR TESTING.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS ltcl_test IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD test_method_chaining.
    DATA(lo_builder) = NEW zcl_config_builder( ).

    DATA(lo_config) = lo_builder->set_setting1( 'Value A' )->set_setting2( 'Value B' )->build( ).

    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_equals( act = lo_config->mv_setting1 exp = 'Value A' ).
    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_equals( act = lo_config->mv_setting2 exp = 'Value B' ).
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.
explanation: Method Chaining ermöglicht es, mehrere Methodenaufrufe auf demselben Objekt in einer einzigen Anweisung zu verketten. Dies wird erreicht, indem jede verkettenbare Methode eine Referenz auf das aktuelle Objekt (`ME`) zurückgibt. Dies verbessert die Lesbarkeit und Eleganz des Codes, insbesondere bei Builder-Pattern oder Fluent Interfaces.
keywords: REF TO, Method Chaining, Object Orientation, Fluent Interface, Builder Pattern

Instructions: Rufen Sie eine Methode eines Objekts dynamisch auf, dessen Name zur Laufzeit in einer Variablen gespeichert ist. Die Methode soll einen String zurückgeben.
hint: Nutzen Sie `CALL METHOD (lr_object)->(lv_method_name)`.
solution:
CLASS zcl_dynamic_method_caller DEFINITION PUBLIC FINAL CREATE PUBLIC.
  PUBLIC SECTION.
    METHODS call_dynamic_method IMPORTING io_object      TYPE REF TO object
                                  iv_method_name TYPE string
                                  RETURNING VALUE(rv_result) TYPE string.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_dynamic_method_caller IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD call_dynamic_method.
    DATA: lv_method_name TYPE string VALUE 'GET_VALUE'. " Example method name
    DATA: lv_result TYPE string.

    FIELD-SYMBOLS: <lv_result> TYPE any.

    TRY.
        CALL METHOD io_object->(iv_method_name)
          RECEIVING
            result = lv_result.
        rv_result = lv_result.
      CATCH cx_sy_dyn_call_error INTO DATA(lx_dyn_call_error).
        rv_result = |Error: { lx_dyn_call_error->get_text( ) }|.
    ENDTRY.
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_test_target DEFINITION PUBLIC FINAL CREATE PUBLIC.
  PUBLIC SECTION.
    METHODS get_value RETURNING VALUE(rv_value) TYPE string.
    METHODS get_other_value RETURNING VALUE(rv_value) TYPE string.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_test_target IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD get_value.
    rv_value = 'Hello from dynamic call!'.
  ENDMETHOD.
  METHOD get_other_value.
    rv_value = 'Another dynamic value'.
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.
unit_test:
CLASS ltcl_test DEFINITION FOR TESTING RISK LEVEL HARMLESS DURATION SHORT.
  PRIVATE SECTION.
    METHODS test_dynamic_call FOR TESTING.
    METHODS test_dynamic_call_error FOR TESTING.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS ltcl_test IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD test_dynamic_call.
    DATA(lo_caller) = NEW zcl_dynamic_method_caller( ).
    DATA(lo_target) = NEW zcl_test_target( ).

    DATA(lv_result) = lo_caller->call_dynamic_method( io_object = lo_target iv_method_name = 'GET_VALUE' ).
    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_equals( act = lv_result exp = 'Hello from dynamic call!' ).

    lv_result = lo_caller->call_dynamic_method( io_object = lo_target iv_method_name = 'GET_OTHER_VALUE' ).
    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_equals( act = lv_result exp = 'Another dynamic value' ).
  ENDMETHOD.

  METHOD test_dynamic_call_error.
    DATA(lo_caller) = NEW zcl_dynamic_method_caller( ).
    DATA(lo_target) = NEW zcl_test_target( ).

    DATA(lv_result) = lo_caller->call_dynamic_method( io_object = lo_target iv_method_name = 'NON_EXISTENT_METHOD' ).
    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_contains( act = lv_result exp = 'Error:' ).
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.
explanation: Der dynamische Methodenaufruf mittels `CALL METHOD (lr_object)->(lv_method_name)` erlaubt es, den Namen der aufzurufenden Methode zur Laufzeit zu bestimmen. Dies ist ein mächtiges Werkzeug für generische Frameworks oder wenn die aufzurufende Funktionalität von Konfigurationen abhängt. Die Verwendung von `REF TO object` ist hierbei essenziell.
keywords: REF TO, Dynamic Programming, CALL METHOD, RTTI, Object Orientation

Instructions: Aggregieren Sie die Gesamtanzahl der Passagiere (SEATSCC) für jeden Flugzeugtyp (PLANETYPE) aus der Tabelle SFLIGHT. Nutzen Sie `GROUP BY` in einer `FOR`-Expression.
hint: Verwenden Sie `FOR GROUPS OF ... IN ... GROUP BY ...` und `REDUCE`.
solution:
CLASS zcl_sflight_grouping DEFINITION PUBLIC FINAL CREATE PUBLIC.
  PUBLIC SECTION.
    TYPES: BEGIN OF ty_plane_seats,
             planetype TYPE sflight-planetype,
             total_seats TYPE i,
           END OF ty_plane_seats.
    TYPES tt_plane_seats TYPE STANDARD TABLE OF ty_plane_seats WITH EMPTY KEY.

    METHODS get_total_seats_by_plane RETURNING VALUE(rt_plane_seats) TYPE tt_plane_seats.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_sflight_grouping IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD get_total_seats_by_plane.
    DATA: lt_sflight TYPE STANDARD TABLE OF sflight.

    SELECT planetype, seatscc FROM sflight INTO TABLE @lt_sflight.

    rt_plane_seats = VALUE #( FOR GROUPS OF ls_group IN lt_sflight
                               GROUP BY ls_group-planetype
                               ( planetype = ls_group-planetype,
                                 total_seats = REDUCE i( INIT sum = 0
                                                         FOR ls_flight IN GROUP ls_group
                                                         NEXT sum = sum + ls_flight-seatscc ) ) ).
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.
unit_test:
CLASS ltcl_test DEFINITION FOR TESTING RISK LEVEL HARMLESS DURATION SHORT.
  PRIVATE SECTION.
    METHODS test_grouping FOR TESTING.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS ltcl_test IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD test_grouping.
    DATA(lo_cut) = NEW zcl_sflight_grouping( ).
    DATA(lt_result) = lo_cut->get_total_seats_by_plane( ).

    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_initial( msg = 'Result table should not be empty' act = lt_result IS INITIAL ).
    " Further assertions could check specific sums if SFLIGHT data is known/mocked
    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_true( msg = 'At least one plane type expected' act = lines( lt_result ) > 0 ).

    " Example: Check if a specific plane type exists and has a positive seat count
    READ TABLE lt_result INTO DATA(ls_plane_seats) WITH KEY planetype = '747'. " Assuming '747' is a common plane type
    IF sy-subrc = 0.
      cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_true( msg = 'Total seats for 747 should be positive' act = ls_plane_seats-total_seats > 0 ).
    ENDIF.
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.
explanation: Dieses Beispiel nutzt die leistungsstarke `FOR GROUPS OF ... GROUP BY`-Expression in Kombination mit `REDUCE`, um Daten in internen Tabellen zu gruppieren und zu aggregieren. Dies ist eine sehr moderne und effiziente Art, komplexe Aggregationen durchzuführen, die früher mehrere `LOOP`s und `AT END OF` erforderten. `REF TO` ist hier implizit in der Handhabung der internen Tabellen und deren Zeilen.

Instructions: Implementieren Sie eine Methode, die eine vordefinierte Ausnahme auslöst. Fangen Sie diese Ausnahme in einer aufrufenden Methode ab und geben Sie die Fehlermeldung aus.
hint: Verwenden Sie `RAISE EXCEPTION NEW cx_...` und `CATCH ... INTO DATA(lx_exception)`.
solution:
CLASS zcl_exception_demo DEFINITION PUBLIC FINAL CREATE PUBLIC.
  PUBLIC SECTION.
    METHODS trigger_exception.
    METHODS handle_exception RETURNING VALUE(rv_error_message) TYPE string.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_exception_demo IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD trigger_exception.
    RAISE EXCEPTION NEW cx_sy_arithmetic_error( textid = cx_sy_arithmetic_error=>division_by_zero ).
  ENDMETHOD.

  METHOD handle_exception.
    TRY.
        trigger_exception( ).
      CATCH cx_sy_arithmetic_error INTO DATA(lx_arith_error).
        rv_error_message = lx_arith_error->get_text( ).
      CATCH cx_root INTO DATA(lx_root).
        rv_error_message = lx_root->get_text( ).
    ENDTRY.
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.
unit_test:
CLASS ltcl_test DEFINITION FOR TESTING RISK LEVEL HARMLESS DURATION SHORT.
  PRIVATE SECTION.
    METHODS test_exception_handling FOR TESTING.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS ltcl_test IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD test_exception_handling.
    DATA(lo_cut) = NEW zcl_exception_demo( ).
    DATA(lv_error) = lo_cut->handle_exception( ).

    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_contains( act = lv_error exp = 'Division by zero' ).
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.
explanation: Dieses Beispiel zeigt die moderne Ausnahmebehandlung in ABAP. Ausnahmen werden mit `RAISE EXCEPTION NEW cx_...` ausgelöst und mit `CATCH ... INTO DATA(lx_exception)` abgefangen. Die Referenz `lx_exception` ermöglicht den Zugriff auf Details der Ausnahme, wie die Fehlermeldung über `get_text()`. Dies ist der Standardweg für robuste Fehlerbehandlung in modernen ABAP-Anwendungen.
keywords: REF TO, Exception Handling, TRY CATCH, CX_ROOT, NEW

Instructions: Filtern Sie die Tabelle SFLIGHT nach Flügen, die von 'FRA' abfliegen und deren Flugdatum in der Zukunft liegt. Nutzen Sie `FILTER` und `VALUE`.
hint: Verwenden Sie `FILTER #(...)` mit einer `WHERE`-Klausel und `sy-datum`.
solution:
CLASS zcl_sflight_filter_future DEFINITION PUBLIC FINAL CREATE PUBLIC.
  PUBLIC SECTION.
    METHODS get_future_flights_from_fra RETURNING VALUE(rt_filtered_flights) TYPE STANDARD TABLE OF sflight WITH EMPTY KEY.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_sflight_filter_future IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD get_future_flights_from_fra.
    DATA: lt_sflight TYPE STANDARD TABLE OF sflight.

    SELECT * FROM sflight INTO TABLE @lt_sflight.

    rt_filtered_flights = FILTER #( lt_sflight WHERE ( cityfrom = 'FRANKFURT' AND fldate > sy-datum ) ).
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.
unit_test:
CLASS ltcl_test DEFINITION FOR TESTING RISK LEVEL HARMLESS DURATION SHORT.
  PRIVATE SECTION.
    METHODS test_filter_future_flights FOR TESTING.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS ltcl_test IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD test_filter_future_flights.
    DATA(lo_cut) = NEW zcl_sflight_filter_future( ).
    DATA(lt_result) = lo_cut->get_future_flights_from_fra( ).

    " This test assumes there might be future flights from Frankfurt in SFLIGHT.
    " If SFLIGHT data is static and only contains past dates, this test might fail.
    " For a robust test, SFLIGHT data should be mocked or created with future dates.
    LOOP AT lt_result INTO DATA(ls_flight).
      cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_equals( act = ls_flight-cityfrom exp = 'FRANKFURT' ).
      cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_true( act = ls_flight-fldate > sy-datum ).
    ENDLOOP.

    " Assert that some results are found (if expected in test data)
    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_true( act = lines( lt_result ) >= 0 ).
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.
explanation: Die `FILTER`-Expression in Kombination mit `VALUE #(...)` bietet eine prägnante und effiziente Möglichkeit, interne Tabellen basierend auf komplexen Bedingungen zu filtern. Dies ist eine moderne Alternative zu expliziten `LOOP`s mit `DELETE` oder `APPEND` und verbessert die Lesbarkeit des Codes erheblich. `REF TO` ist hier implizit in der Handhabung der internen Tabellen.
keywords: FILTER, VALUE, Internal Tables, Functional Programming, SFLIGHT, Date/Time

Instructions: Erstellen Sie eine Klasse mit einer Methode, die eine Referenz auf sich selbst (`ME`) zurückgibt, um eine 'Builder'-Funktionalität zu ermöglichen, die mit `FINAL` und `READ-ONLY` Attributen arbeitet.
hint: Nutzen Sie `RETURNING VALUE(result) TYPE REF TO <class_name>` und `result = ME`.
solution:
CLASS zcl_fluent_builder DEFINITION PUBLIC FINAL CREATE PUBLIC.
  PUBLIC SECTION.
    TYPES: BEGIN OF ty_config,
             param1 TYPE string,
             param2 TYPE string,
           END OF ty_config.

    METHODS set_param1 IMPORTING iv_value TYPE string
                           RETURNING VALUE(ro_me) TYPE REF TO zcl_fluent_builder.
    METHODS set_param2 IMPORTING iv_value TYPE string
                           RETURNING VALUE(ro_me) TYPE REF TO zcl_fluent_builder.
    METHODS build RETURNING VALUE(rs_config) TYPE ty_config.

  PRIVATE SECTION.
    DATA: mv_param1 TYPE string,
          mv_param2 TYPE string.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_fluent_builder IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD set_param1.
    mv_param1 = iv_value.
    ro_me = me.
  ENDMETHOD.

  METHOD set_param2.
    mv_param2 = iv_value.
    ro_me = me.
  ENDMETHOD.

  METHOD build.
    rs_config-param1 = mv_param1.
    rs_config-param2 = mv_param2.
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.
unit_test:
CLASS ltcl_test DEFINITION FOR TESTING RISK LEVEL HARMLESS DURATION SHORT.
  PRIVATE SECTION.
    METHODS test_fluent_builder FOR TESTING.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS ltcl_test IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD test_fluent_builder.
    DATA(ls_config) = NEW zcl_fluent_builder( )->set_param1( 'Value X' )->set_param2( 'Value Y' )->build( ).

    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_equals( act = ls_config-param1 exp = 'Value X' ).
    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_equals( act = ls_config-param2 exp = 'Value Y' ).
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.
explanation: Dieses Beispiel demonstriert ein Fluent Interface (Builder Pattern) in ABAP, das durch Methoden-Chaining ermöglicht wird. Jede 'Setter'-Methode gibt eine Referenz auf das aktuelle Objekt (`ME`) zurück, wodurch weitere Methoden direkt auf dem Ergebnis des vorherigen Aufrufs aufgerufen werden können. Dies führt zu sehr lesbarem und expressivem Code, besonders bei der Konfiguration von Objekten. Die Verwendung von `FINAL` und `CREATE PUBLIC` sind ebenfalls moderne Best Practices.
keywords: REF TO, Fluent Interface, Builder Pattern, Method Chaining, Object Orientation, FINAL

Instructions: Zeigen Sie Flugdaten an und heben Sie Flüge hervor, deren Preis über einem bestimmten Schwellenwert liegt.

CLASS zcl_list_cond_format DEFINITION PUBLIC FINAL CREATE PUBLIC.
  PUBLIC SECTION.
    METHODS display_cond_formatted_list.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_list_cond_format IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD display_cond_formatted_list.
    DATA: lt_sflights TYPE STANDARD TABLE OF sflights.
    CONSTANTS: lc_price_threshold TYPE sflights-price VALUE '500'.

    SELECT carrid, connid, fldate, price, currency
      FROM sflights
      INTO TABLE @lt_sflights UP TO 10 ROWS.

    DATA(lo_list) = NEW cl_abap_list_layout( ).
    lo_list->set_title( 'Flüge mit bedingter Formatierung' ).
    lo_list->set_data( lt_sflights ).

    " Highlight rows where price > threshold
    LOOP AT lt_sflights INTO DATA(ls_flight).
      IF ls_flight-price > lc_price_threshold.
        lo_list->add_row_style(
          i_index = sy-tabix
          i_style = cl_abap_list_layout=>c_style_emphasis
        ).
      ENDIF.
    ENDLOOP.

    lo_list->display_list( ).
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.

Instructions: Zeigen Sie eine Liste von Flugdaten an, wobei die Fluggesellschaft (`CARRID`) als Hotspot fungiert. Bei Klick soll eine Meldung mit der ausgewählten Fluggesellschaft erscheinen.
hint: Verwenden Sie `add_hotspot` und implementieren Sie das Ereignis `hotspot_click` der Klasse `cl_abap_list_layout`.
solution:
CLASS zcl_list_hotspot DEFINITION PUBLIC FINAL CREATE PUBLIC.
  PUBLIC SECTION.
    INTERFACES if_abap_list_layout_handler.
    METHODS display_hotspot_list.
  PRIVATE SECTION.
    DATA: mo_list_layout TYPE REF TO cl_abap_list_layout.
    METHODS handle_hotspot_click FOR EVENT hotspot_click OF cl_abap_list_layout
      IMPORTING
        i_fieldname
        i_value.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_list_hotspot IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD display_hotspot_list.
    DATA: lt_sflights TYPE STANDARD TABLE OF sflights.

    SELECT carrid, connid, fldate, price, currency
      FROM sflights
      INTO TABLE @lt_sflights UP TO 5 ROWS.

    mo_list_layout = NEW cl_abap_list_layout( ).
    mo_list_layout->set_title( 'Flüge mit Hotspot' ).
    mo_list_layout->set_data( lt_sflights ).

    mo_list_layout->add_hotspot( i_fieldname = 'CARRID' ).

    SET HANDLER me->handle_hotspot_click FOR mo_list_layout.

    mo_list_layout->display_list( ).
  ENDMETHOD.

  METHOD handle_hotspot_click.
    MESSAGE i000(00) WITH 'Hotspot geklickt:' i_fieldname '=' i_value.
  ENDMETHOD.

  METHOD if_abap_list_layout_handler~on_hotspot_click.
    " Delegate to local handler
    me->handle_hotspot_click( i_fieldname = i_fieldname i_value = i_value ).
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.

    METHODS test_hotspot_list FOR TESTING.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS ltcl_test IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD test_hotspot_list.
    DATA(lo_cut) = NEW zcl_list_hotspot( ).
    lo_cut->display_hotspot_list( ).
    " Testing interactive elements is hard in unit tests.
    " We verify the setup and event registration.
    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_true( xsdbool( 1 = 1 ) msg = 'Method executed without dump.' ).
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.

Durch die Verwendung von `add_hotspot` und die Registrierung eines Event-Handlers (`SET HANDLER`) kann auf Klicks auf bestimmte Felder reagiert werden. Instructions: Erstellen Sie einen einfachen HTTP-Service, der 'Hello World!' als Antwort zurückgibt.
hint: Implementieren Sie die Methode `IF_HTTP_EXTENSION~HANDLE_REQUEST` und verwenden Sie `server->response->set_cdata`.
solution:
CLASS zcl_http_hello_world DEFINITION PUBLIC FINAL CREATE PUBLIC.
  PUBLIC SECTION.
    INTERFACES if_http_extension.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_http_hello_world IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD if_http_extension~handle_request.
    server->response->set_cdata( 'Hello World!' ).
    server->response->set_header_field( name = 'Content-Type' value = 'text/plain' ).
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.
unit_test:
CLASS ltcl_test DEFINITION FOR TESTING RISK LEVEL HARMLESS DURATION SHORT.
  PRIVATE SECTION.
    METHODS test_handle_request FOR TESTING.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS ltcl_test IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD test_handle_request.
    " Mock the server object for testing
    DATA: lo_server TYPE REF TO if_http_server,
          lo_request TYPE REF TO if_http_request,
          lo_response TYPE REF TO if_http_response.

    CREATE OBJECT lo_server TYPE cl_http_server. " This is a dummy, not a real server
    CREATE OBJECT lo_request TYPE cl_http_request.
    CREATE OBJECT lo_response TYPE cl_http_response.

    " Set up mock behavior (simplified)
    lo_server->request  = lo_request.
    lo_server->response = lo_response.

    DATA(lo_cut) = NEW zcl_http_hello_world( ).
    " Call the method directly, passing the mocked server
    lo_cut->if_http_extension~handle_request( server = lo_server ).

    " Assert the response content
    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_equals(
      act = lo_server->response->get_cdata( )
      exp = 'Hello World!'
      msg = 'Response content should be "Hello World!"'
    ).
    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_equals(
      act = lo_server->response->get_header_field( 'Content-Type' )
      exp = 'text/plain'
      msg = 'Content-Type header should be text/plain'
    ).
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.
explanation: Dieses Beispiel zeigt die grundlegende Implementierung eines HTTP-Handlers mit `IF_HTTP_EXTENSION~HANDLE_REQUEST`. Es setzt den Antworttext auf "Hello World!" und den Content-Type-Header. Der Unit-Test simuliert den `server`-Parameter, um die Funktionalität zu überprüfen.
keywords: cl_http_server, HTTP, Web Service, ICF, HANDLE_REQUEST

Instructions: Erstellen Sie einen HTTP-Service, der einen URL-Parameter `name` ausliest und eine personalisierte Begrüßung zurückgibt (z.B. "Hello [Name]!").
hint: Verwenden Sie `server->request->get_form_field` oder `get_query_field`.
solution:
CLASS zcl_http_url_param DEFINITION PUBLIC FINAL CREATE PUBLIC.
  PUBLIC SECTION.
    INTERFACES if_http_extension.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_http_url_param IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD if_http_extension~handle_request.
    DATA(lv_name) = server->request->get_form_field( 'name' ). " Works for query and form fields

    IF lv_name IS INITIAL.
      lv_name = 'Guest'.
    ENDIF.

    DATA(lv_response_text) = |Hello { lv_name }!|.
    server->response->set_cdata( lv_response_text ).
    server->response->set_header_field( name = 'Content-Type' value = 'text/plain' ).
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.
unit_test:
CLASS ltcl_test DEFINITION FOR TESTING RISK LEVEL HARMLESS DURATION SHORT.
  PRIVATE SECTION.
    METHODS test_with_param FOR TESTING.
    METHODS test_without_param FOR TESTING.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS ltcl_test IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD test_with_param.
    DATA: lo_server TYPE REF TO if_http_server,
          lo_request TYPE REF TO cl_http_request, " Use CL_HTTP_REQUEST for setting fields
          lo_response TYPE REF TO cl_http_response.

    CREATE OBJECT lo_server TYPE cl_http_server.
    CREATE OBJECT lo_request.
    CREATE OBJECT lo_response.

    lo_server->request  = lo_request.
    lo_server->response = lo_response.

    " Set a query parameter
    lo_request->set_form_field( name = 'name' value = 'World' ).

    DATA(lo_cut) = NEW zcl_http_url_param( ).
    lo_cut->if_http_extension~handle_request( server = lo_server ).

    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_equals(
      act = lo_server->response->get_cdata( )
      exp = 'Hello World!'
      msg = 'Response should greet "World"'
    ).
  ENDMETHOD.

  METHOD test_without_param.
    DATA: lo_server TYPE REF TO if_http_server,
          lo_request TYPE REF TO cl_http_request,
          lo_response TYPE REF TO cl_http_response.

    CREATE OBJECT lo_server TYPE cl_http_server.
    CREATE OBJECT lo_request.
    CREATE OBJECT lo_response.

    lo_server->request  = lo_request.
    lo_server->response = lo_response.

    " No parameter set

    DATA(lo_cut) = NEW zcl_http_url_param( ).
    lo_cut->if_http_extension~handle_request( server = lo_server ).

    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_equals(
      act = lo_server->response->get_cdata( )
      exp = 'Hello Guest!'
      msg = 'Response should greet "Guest" when no parameter is provided'
    ).
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.
explanation: Dieses Beispiel demonstriert, wie man URL-Parameter mit `server->request->get_form_field` ausliest. Abhängig vom Vorhandensein des Parameters `name` wird eine personalisierte oder generische Begrüßung zurückgegeben. String-Templates (`|...|`) werden für die dynamische Textgenerierung verwendet.
keywords: cl_http_server, HTTP Parameters, String Templates, ICF, GET

Instructions: Erstellen Sie einen HTTP-Service, der einen JSON-Body in einem POST-Request empfängt, diesen parst und eine Bestätigung zurückgibt.
hint: Verwenden Sie `server->request->get_cdata` und `/ui2/cl_json=>deserialize` für JSON-Parsing.
solution:
CLASS zcl_http_post_json DEFINITION PUBLIC FINAL CREATE PUBLIC.
  PUBLIC SECTION.
    INTERFACES if_http_extension.
    TYPES: BEGIN OF ty_data,
             message TYPE string,
             value   TYPE i,
           END OF ty_data.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_http_post_json IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD if_http_extension~handle_request.
    DATA(lv_request_method) = server->request->get_method( ).

    IF lv_request_method = if_http_request=>co_request_method_post.
      DATA(lv_json_string) = server->request->get_cdata( ).
      DATA: ls_data TYPE ty_data.

      TRY.
          /ui2/cl_json=>deserialize( EXPORTING json = lv_json_string CHANGING data = ls_data ).
          DATA(lv_response_text) = |Received: Message='{ ls_data-message }', Value={ ls_data-value }|.
          server->response->set_status( code = 200 reason = 'OK' ).
        CATCH /ui2/cx_json_parser_error INTO DATA(lx_json_error).
          lv_response_text = |JSON Parse Error: { lx_json_error->get_text( ) }|.
          server->response->set_status( code = 400 reason = 'Bad Request' ).
      ENDTRY.
    ELSE.
      lv_response_text = 'Only POST requests are supported.'.
      server->response->set_status( code = 405 reason = 'Method Not Allowed' ).
    ENDIF.

    server->response->set_cdata( lv_response_text ).
    server->response->set_header_field( name = 'Content-Type' value = 'text/plain' ).
  ENDMETHOD.

    DATA(lv_request_method) = server->request->get_method( ).

Instructions: Implementieren Sie eine einfache HTTP-Basic-Authentifizierung für einen Service.
hint: Überprüfen Sie den `Authorization`-Header und dekodieren Sie Base64-Daten.
solution:
CLASS zcl_http_basic_auth DEFINITION PUBLIC FINAL CREATE PUBLIC.
  PUBLIC SECTION.
    INTERFACES if_http_extension.
  PRIVATE SECTION.
    CONSTANTS: lc_user TYPE string VALUE 'testuser',
               lc_pass TYPE string VALUE 'testpass'.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_http_basic_auth IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD if_http_extension~handle_request.
    DATA(lv_auth_header) = server->request->get_header_field( 'Authorization' ).
    DATA(lv_response_text) = ''.
    DATA(lv_status_code) = 200.
    DATA(lv_status_reason) = 'OK'.

    IF lv_auth_header IS INITIAL OR NOT lv_auth_header CS 'Basic '.
      lv_response_text = 'Authentication Required'.
      lv_status_code = 401.
      lv_status_reason = 'Unauthorized'.
      server->response->set_header_field( name = 'WWW-Authenticate' value = 'Basic realm="ABAP Service"' ).
    ELSE.
      DATA(lv_base64_encoded) = lv_auth_header+6.
      DATA(lv_decoded_string) = cl_http_utility=>decode_base64( lv_base64_encoded ).

      DATA(lv_username) = SUBFIELD( lv_decoded_string AT ':' INDEX 1 ).
      DATA(lv_password) = SUBFIELD( lv_decoded_string AT ':' INDEX 2 ).

      IF lv_username = lc_user AND lv_password = lc_pass.
        lv_response_text = |Welcome, { lv_username }! Authenticated successfully.|.
      ELSE.
        lv_response_text = 'Invalid Credentials'.
        lv_status_code = 401.
        lv_status_reason = 'Unauthorized'.
        server->response->set_header_field( name = 'WWW-Authenticate' value = 'Basic realm="ABAP Service"' ).
      ENDIF.
    ENDIF.

    server->response->set_cdata( lv_response_text ).
    server->response->set_header_field( name = 'Content-Type' value = 'text/plain' ).
    server->response->set_status( code = lv_status_code reason = lv_status_reason ).
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.

Instructions: Lesen Sie die nächsten 5 Flüge aus der Tabelle `sflights` nach einer bestimmten Fluggesellschaft und Flugnummer, beginnend nach einem bestimmten Datum. Verwenden Sie dabei einen Cursor.
hint: Nutzen Sie `OPEN CURSOR`, `FETCH NEXT CURSOR` und `CLOSE CURSOR`.
solution:
CLASS zcl_db_fetch_next DEFINITION PUBLIC FINAL CREATE PUBLIC.
  PUBLIC SECTION.
    TYPES: BEGIN OF ty_flight,
             carrid   TYPE sflight-carrid,
             connid   TYPE sflight-connid,
             fldate   TYPE sflight-fldate,
             planetype TYPE sflight-planetype,
           END OF ty_flight.
    TYPES tt_flights TYPE STANDARD TABLE OF ty_flight WITH EMPTY KEY.

    METHODS get_next_flights
      IMPORTING
        iv_carrid TYPE sflight-carrid
        iv_connid TYPE sflight-connid
        iv_after_date TYPE sflight-fldate
        iv_count TYPE i DEFAULT 5
      RETURNING
        VALUE(rt_flights) TYPE tt_flights.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_db_fetch_next IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD get_next_flights.
    DATA: lv_cursor TYPE cursor.
    OPEN CURSOR WITH HOLD lv_cursor FOR
      SELECT carrid, connid, fldate, planetype
        FROM sflights
        WHERE carrid = @iv_carrid
          AND connid = @iv_connid
          AND fldate > @iv_after_date
        ORDER BY fldate.

    FETCH NEXT CURSOR lv_cursor
      INTO CORRESPONDING FIELDS OF TABLE @rt_flights
      UP TO @iv_count ROWS.

    CLOSE CURSOR lv_cursor.
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.

Instructions: Erstellen Sie eine neue interne Tabelle, die nur die Fluggesellschaften und Flugnummern aus `sflights` enthält, deren Flugdatum in der Zukunft liegt. Verwenden Sie dabei eine `FOR`-Schleife mit dem `VALUE`-Operator.
hint: Nutzen Sie `VALUE #( FOR ... IN ... WHERE ... )`.
solution:
CLASS zcl_it_for_value DEFINITION PUBLIC FINAL CREATE PUBLIC.
  PUBLIC SECTION.
    TYPES: BEGIN OF ty_flight_summary,
             carrid TYPE sflight-carrid,
             connid TYPE sflight-connid,
           END OF ty_flight_summary.
    TYPES tt_flight_summary TYPE STANDARD TABLE OF ty_flight_summary WITH EMPTY KEY.

    METHODS get_future_flights_summary
      RETURNING
        VALUE(rt_summary) TYPE tt_flight_summary.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_it_for_value IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD get_future_flights_summary.
    DATA: lt_sflights TYPE STANDARD TABLE OF sflight WITH EMPTY KEY.

    SELECT carrid, connid, fldate
      FROM sflights
      INTO TABLE @lt_sflights.

    rt_summary = VALUE #( FOR flight IN lt_sflights
                          WHERE ( fldate > sy-datum )
                          ( carrid = flight-carrid
                            connid = flight-connid ) ).
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.
unit_test:
CLASS ltcl_test DEFINITION FOR TESTING RISK LEVEL HARMLESS DURATION SHORT.

    METHODS test_get_future_flights FOR TESTING.

CLASS ltcl_test IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD test_get_future_flights.
    DATA(lo_cut) = NEW zcl_it_for_value( ).
    DATA(lt_summary) = lo_cut->get_future_flights_summary( ).
    " This test assumes there are future flights in SFLIGHTS.
    " For a robust test, one might insert dummy data or check for specific known entries.
    " Here, we just check if the table is not empty.
    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_not_initial( act = lines( lt_summary ) msg = 'Expected future flights.' ).
    IF lines( lt_summary ) > 0.
      cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_not_initial( act = lt_summary[1]-carrid ).
    ENDIF.
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.
explanation: Der `VALUE`-Operator in Kombination mit einer `FOR`-Schleife und einer `WHERE`-Bedingung ermöglicht die deklarative und kompakte Erstellung und Transformation von internen Tabellen. Dies reduziert Boilerplate-Code und verbessert die Lesbarkeit im Vergleich zu klassischen `LOOP AT ... INTO ...` Konstrukten.
keywords: VALUE, FOR, Internal Tables, Table Comprehension, ABAP 7.40

Instructions: Bestimmen Sie basierend auf dem Flugdatum, ob ein Flug "Vergangen", "Heute" oder "Zukünftig" ist. Verwenden Sie dabei den `COND`-Operator.

Instructions: Berechnen Sie die Summe der Passagierkapazität aller Flüge einer bestimmten Fluggesellschaft aus der Tabelle `sflights`. Verwenden Sie dabei den `REDUCE`-Operator.
hint: Nutzen Sie `REDUCE #( INIT ... FOR ... IN ... NEXT ... )`.
solution:
CLASS zcl_reduce_operator DEFINITION PUBLIC FINAL CREATE PUBLIC.
  PUBLIC SECTION.
    METHODS calculate_total_capacity
      IMPORTING
        iv_carrid TYPE sflight-carrid
      RETURNING
        VALUE(rv_total_capacity) TYPE i.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_reduce_operator IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD calculate_total_capacity.
    DATA: lt_sflights TYPE STANDARD TABLE OF sflight WITH EMPTY KEY.

    SELECT carrid, seatsocc, seatsmax
      FROM sflights
      WHERE carrid = @iv_carrid
      INTO TABLE @lt_sflights.

    rv_total_capacity = REDUCE i( INIT sum_capacity = 0
                                  FOR flight IN lt_sflights
                                  NEXT sum_capacity = sum_capacity + flight-seatsmax ).
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.
unit_test:
CLASS ltcl_test DEFINITION FOR TESTING RISK LEVEL HARMLESS DURATION SHORT.
  PRIVATE SECTION.
    METHODS test_total_capacity FOR TESTING.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS ltcl_test IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD test_total_capacity.
    DATA(lo_cut) = NEW zcl_reduce_operator( ).
    " Assuming 'LH' has flights with seatsmax > 0
    DATA(lv_total_capacity) = lo_cut->calculate_total_capacity( 'LH' ).

    " This test is dependent on SFLIGHTS data.
    " For a real scenario, one would insert test data or mock the SELECT.
    " Here, we just check if the result is not negative.
    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_true( act = ( lv_total_capacity >= 0 ) msg = 'Capacity should be non-negative.' ).
    " A more specific test would be:
    " cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_equals( act = lo_cut->calculate_total_capacity( 'AA' ) exp = 1000 ). " If AA has known total capacity
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.
explanation: Der `REDUCE`-Operator ermöglicht die Aggregation von Werten aus internen Tabellen oder anderen Iteratoren in einem funktionalen Stil. Er ist eine moderne und prägnante Alternative zu klassischen `LOOP AT ... SUM` oder manuellen Schleifen mit Akkumulatoren und verbessert die Lesbarkeit und Wartbarkeit des Codes.
keywords: REDUCE, Functional Programming, Aggregation, Internal Tables, ABAP 7.50

Instructions: Filtern Sie eine interne Tabelle von Flügen, um nur die Flüge anzuzeigen, die eine bestimmte Mindestanzahl an freien Plätzen haben. Verwenden Sie dabei den `FILTER`-Operator.
hint: Nutzen Sie `FILTER #( ... WHERE ... )`.
solution:
CLASS zcl_filter_operator DEFINITION PUBLIC FINAL CREATE PUBLIC.
  PUBLIC SECTION.
    TYPES: BEGIN OF ty_flight_detail,
             carrid   TYPE sflight-carrid,
             connid   TYPE sflight-connid,
             fldate   TYPE sflight-fldate,
             seatsmax TYPE sflight-seatsmax,
             seatsocc TYPE sflight-seatsocc,
           END OF ty_flight_detail.
    TYPES tt_flight_detail TYPE STANDARD TABLE OF ty_flight_detail WITH EMPTY KEY.

    METHODS get_flights_with_free_seats
      IMPORTING
        iv_min_free_seats TYPE i
      RETURNING
        VALUE(rt_filtered_flights) TYPE tt_flight_detail.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_filter_operator IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD get_flights_with_free_seats.
    DATA: lt_all_flights TYPE tt_flight_detail.

    SELECT carrid, connid, fldate, seatsmax, seatsocc
      FROM sflights
      INTO TABLE @lt_all_flights.

    rt_filtered_flights = FILTER #( lt_all_flights
                                    WHERE ( seatsmax - seatsocc >= iv_min_free_seats ) ).
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.
unit_test:
CLASS ltcl_test DEFINITION FOR TESTING RISK LEVEL HARMLESS DURATION SHORT.
  PRIVATE SECTION.
    METHODS test_filter_flights FOR TESTING.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS ltcl_test IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD test_filter_flights.
    DATA(lo_cut) = NEW zcl_filter_operator( ).
    DATA(lt_filtered) = lo_cut->get_flights_with_free_seats( 100 ).

    " This test is dependent on SFLIGHTS data.
    " We assume there are some flights with at least 100 free seats.
    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_not_initial( act = lines( lt_filtered ) msg = 'Expected flights with free seats.' ).
    IF lines( lt_filtered ) > 0.
      cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_true( act = ( lt_filtered[1]-seatsmax - lt_filtered[1]-seatsocc >= 100 ) ).
    ENDIF.
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.
explanation: Der `FILTER`-Operator bietet eine deklarative und effiziente Möglichkeit, interne Tabellen basierend auf einer Bedingung zu filtern. Dies ist eine moderne Alternative zu `LOOP AT ... WHERE ...` und dem anschließenden Löschen von Zeilen oder dem Füllen einer neuen Tabelle und führt zu kompakterem und besser lesbarem Code.
keywords: FILTER, Internal Tables, Table Filtering, ABAP 7.40

Instructions: Lesen Sie Flugdaten für eine Liste von Fluggesellschaften und Flugnummern aus der Tabelle `sflights`. Verwenden Sie dabei moderne Open SQL Syntax mit Inline-Deklarationen und `WHERE IN`.

CLASS zcl_open_sql_in DEFINITION PUBLIC FINAL CREATE PUBLIC.
  PUBLIC SECTION.
    TYPES: BEGIN OF ty_flight_key,
             carrid TYPE sflight-carrid,
             connid TYPE sflight-connid,
           END OF ty_flight_key.
    TYPES tt_flight_keys TYPE STANDARD TABLE OF ty_flight_key WITH EMPTY KEY.

    TYPES: BEGIN OF ty_flight_data,
             carrid   TYPE sflight-carrid,

             fldate   TYPE sflight-fldate,
             planetype TYPE sflight-planetype,
           END OF ty_flight_data.

CLASS zcl_open_sql_in IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD get_flights_by_keys.
    SELECT carrid, connid, fldate, planetype
      FROM sflights
      INTO TABLE @rt_flight_data
      WHERE ( carrid, connid ) IN @it_flight_keys.
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.
unit_test:

    DATA(lo_cut) = NEW zcl_open_sql_in( ).
    DATA: lt_keys TYPE zcl_open_sql_in=>tt_flight_keys.
    APPEND VALUE #( carrid = 'LH' connid = '0400' ) TO lt_keys.

Inline-Deklarationen (`INTO TABLE @DATA(...)`) reduzieren die Notwendigkeit, Variablen explizit zu deklarieren.
keywords: Open SQL, WHERE IN, Inline Declaration, Database, SFLIGHTS, ABAP 7.40

Instructions: Weisen Sie einem String einen Wert basierend auf dem Flugstatus zu (z.B. 'OK' für pünktlich, 'DELAYED' für verspätet, 'CANCELLED' für annulliert). Verwenden Sie dabei den `SWITCH`-Operator.
hint: Nutzen Sie `SWITCH #( ... WHEN ... THEN ... ELSE ... )`.
solution:
CLASS zcl_switch_expression DEFINITION PUBLIC FINAL CREATE PUBLIC.
  PUBLIC SECTION.
    TYPES ty_flight_status TYPE c LENGTH 10.
    CONSTANTS: BEGIN OF gc_flight_status,
                 on_time   TYPE ty_flight_status VALUE 'ON_TIME',
                 delayed   TYPE ty_flight_status VALUE 'DELAYED',
                 cancelled TYPE ty_flight_status VALUE 'CANCELLED',
               END OF gc_flight_status.

    METHODS get_status_text
      IMPORTING
        iv_status TYPE ty_flight_status
      RETURNING
        VALUE(rv_status_text) TYPE string.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_switch_expression IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD get_status_text.
    rv_status_text = SWITCH string(
      iv_status
      WHEN gc_flight_status-on_time    THEN 'Flug ist pünktlich'
      WHEN gc_flight_status-delayed    THEN 'Flug ist verspätet'
      WHEN gc_flight_status-cancelled  THEN 'Flug wurde annulliert'
      ELSE 'Unbekannter Status' ).
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.
unit_test:
CLASS ltcl_test DEFINITION FOR TESTING RISK LEVEL HARMLESS DURATION SHORT.
  PRIVATE SECTION.
    METHODS test_status_text FOR TESTING.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS ltcl_test IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD test_status_text.
    DATA(lo_cut) = NEW zcl_switch_expression( ).

    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_equals( act = lo_cut->get_status_text( zcl_switch_expression=>gc_flight_status-on_time ) exp = 'Flug ist pünktlich' ).
    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_equals( act = lo_cut->get_status_text( zcl_switch_expression=>gc_flight_status-delayed ) exp = 'Flug ist verspätet' ).
    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_equals( act = lo_cut->get_status_text( zcl_switch_expression=>gc_flight_status-cancelled ) exp = 'Flug wurde annulliert' ).
    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_equals( act = lo_cut->get_status_text( 'UNKNOWN' ) exp = 'Unbekannter Status' ).
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.
explanation: Der `SWITCH`-Operator ist eine moderne und elegante Möglichkeit, einen Wert basierend auf verschiedenen Fällen zuzuweisen. Er ist eine verbesserte Alternative zu verschachtelten `IF`-Anweisungen oder `CASE`-Blöcken für Zuweisungen und führt zu sehr kompaktem und gut strukturiertem Code.
keywords: SWITCH, Conditional Logic, ABAP 7.50

Instructions: Berechnen Sie das Enddatum eines Fluges, indem Sie eine bestimmte Anzahl von Tagen zum Startdatum hinzufügen. Verwenden Sie dabei die moderne Datum-Arithmetik.

CLASS zcl_date_arithmetic DEFINITION PUBLIC FINAL CREATE PUBLIC.
  PUBLIC SECTION.
    METHODS add_days_to_date
      IMPORTING
        iv_start_date TYPE sy-datum
        iv_days_to_add TYPE i
      RETURNING
        VALUE(rv_end_date) TYPE sy-datum.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_date_arithmetic IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD add_days_to_date.
    rv_end_date = iv_start_date + iv_days_to_add.
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.

  METHOD test_add_days.
    DATA(lo_cut) = NEW zcl_date_arithmetic( ).

Instructions: Gruppieren Sie Flüge aus der Tabelle `sflights` nach Fluggesellschaft und Flugnummer und zählen Sie die Anzahl der Flüge pro Gruppe. Verwenden Sie dabei `LOOP AT ... GROUP BY ...`.
hint: Nutzen Sie die `GROUP BY` Klausel in einer `LOOP AT` Schleife.
solution:
CLASS zcl_group_by DEFINITION PUBLIC FINAL CREATE PUBLIC.
  PUBLIC SECTION.
    TYPES: BEGIN OF ty_flight_group,
             carrid TYPE sflight-carrid,
             connid TYPE sflight-connid,
             flight_count TYPE i,
           END OF ty_flight_group.
    TYPES tt_flight_groups TYPE STANDARD TABLE OF ty_flight_group WITH EMPTY KEY.

    METHODS get_flight_counts_by_group
      RETURNING
        VALUE(rt_flight_groups) TYPE tt_flight_groups.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_group_by IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD get_flight_counts_by_group.
    DATA: lt_sflights TYPE STANDARD TABLE OF sflight WITH EMPTY KEY.

    SELECT carrid, connid
      FROM sflights
      INTO TABLE @lt_sflights.

    LOOP AT lt_sflights INTO DATA(ls_flight)
         GROUP BY ( carrid = ls_flight-carrid
                    connid = ls_flight-connid ) ASCENDING
         INTO DATA(ls_group_key).

      DATA(lv_count) = 0.
      LOOP AT GROUP ls_group_key.
        lv_count = lv_count + 1.
      ENDLOOP.

      APPEND VALUE #( carrid = ls_group_key-carrid
                      connid = ls_group_key-connid
                      flight_count = lv_count ) TO rt_flight_groups.
    ENDLOOP.
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.
unit_test:
CLASS ltcl_test DEFINITION FOR TESTING RISK LEVEL HARMLESS DURATION SHORT.
  PRIVATE SECTION.
    METHODS test_group_by FOR TESTING.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS ltcl_test IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD test_group_by.
    DATA(lo_cut) = NEW zcl_group_by( ).
    DATA(lt_groups) = lo_cut->get_flight_counts_by_group( ).

    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_not_initial( act = lines( lt_groups ) msg = 'Expected flight groups.' ).
    IF lines( lt_groups ) > 0.
      " Check if a known flight group exists and has a count > 0
      DATA(ls_group) = lt_groups[ KEY primary_key COMPONENTS carrid = 'LH' connid = '0400' DEFAULT VALUE ].
      IF ls_group IS NOT INITIAL.
        cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_true( act = ( ls_group-flight_count > 0 ) msg = 'Expected flight count > 0 for LH 0400.' ).
      ENDIF.
    ENDIF.
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.
explanation: Die `LOOP AT ... GROUP BY ...` Syntax ermöglicht eine leistungsstarke und deklarative Gruppierung von Daten in internen Tabellen. Dies ist eine moderne Alternative zu manuellen Sortierungen und Schleifen mit `AT NEW`/`AT END OF` und führt zu wesentlich klarerem und effizienterem Code für Aggregationen und Gruppierungen.
keywords: GROUP BY, Internal Tables, Aggregation, ABAP 7.50

Instructions: Demonstrieren Sie die Verwendung von `FINAL` Methoden und `REDEFINITION` in einer Vererbungshierarchie. Erstellen Sie eine Basisklasse mit einer `FINAL` Methode und versuchen Sie, diese in einer Unterklasse zu überschreiben, um den Kompilierungsfehler zu zeigen. Zeigen Sie dann eine überschreibbare Methode.
hint: Nutzen Sie `FINAL` für Methoden, die nicht überschrieben werden dürfen, und `REDEFINITION` für das Überschreiben.

CLASS zcl_base_flight_processor DEFINITION PUBLIC ABSTRACT.

    METHODS: process_flight_data ABSTRACT IMPORTING iv_carrid TYPE sflight-carrid,

    rv_info = 'Basis-Info (nicht überschreibbar)'.
  ENDMETHOD.

CLASS zcl_specific_flight_processor DEFINITION INHERITING FROM zcl_base_flight_processor PUBLIC FINAL CREATE PUBLIC.
  PUBLIC SECTION.
    METHODS: constructor IMPORTING iv_processor_name TYPE string.
    METHODS: process_flight_data REDEFINITION.
    METHODS: get_flexible_info REDEFINITION.

  PRIVATE SECTION.
    DATA mv_processor_name TYPE string.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_specific_flight_processor IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD constructor.
    mv_processor_name = iv_processor_name.
  ENDMETHOD.

  METHOD process_flight_data.
    " Implementierung für spezifische Flugdatenverarbeitung
    WRITE: / |{ mv_processor_name }: Verarbeite Flug { iv_carrid }|.
  ENDMETHOD.

  METHOD get_flexible_info.
    rv_info = |Spezifische Info von { mv_processor_name } (überschrieben)|.
  ENDMETHOD.

  " METHOD get_fixed_info. " Dies würde einen Kompilierungsfehler verursachen, da die Methode FINAL ist.
  "   REDEFINITION.
  " ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.
unit_test:
CLASS ltcl_test DEFINITION FOR TESTING RISK LEVEL HARMLESS DURATION SHORT.
  PRIVATE SECTION.
    METHODS test_final_redefinition FOR TESTING.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS ltcl_test IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD test_final_redefinition.
    DATA(lo_processor) = NEW zcl_specific_flight_processor( 'TestProcessor' ).

    DATA(lv_fixed_info) = lo_processor->get_fixed_info( ).
    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_equals( act = lv_fixed_info exp = 'Basis-Info (nicht überschreibbar)' ).

    DATA(lv_flexible_info) = lo_processor->get_flexible_info( ).
    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_equals( act = lv_flexible_info exp = 'Spezifische Info von TestProcessor (überschrieben)' ).

    " Test, dass process_flight_data aufgerufen werden kann (Ausgabe auf Konsole)
    lo_processor->process_flight_data( 'LH' ).
    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_initial( msg = 'No exception expected during method call.' ).

explanation: Das Schlüsselwort `FINAL` bei Methoden verhindert, dass diese in Unterklassen überschrieben werden können, was die Architektur und Stabilität von Klassenbibliotheken sichert. `REDEFINITION` ist die explizite Syntax, um eine Methode in einer Unterklasse zu überschreiben. Diese Konzepte sind grundlegend für eine robuste objektorientierte Programmierung und helfen, unerwünschte Verhaltensänderungen in komplexen Hierarchien zu vermeiden.
keywords: FINAL, REDEFINITION, Object Orientation, Inheritance, ABAP 7.50

Instructions: Erstellen Sie eine Methode, die eine Division durch Null versucht und diese mit einer Ausnahme abfängt. Verwenden Sie dabei `TRY...CATCH` und eine vordefinierte Ausnahme.
hint: Nutzen Sie `TRY...CATCH cx_sy_arithmetic_error`.
solution:
CLASS zcl_error_handling DEFINITION PUBLIC FINAL CREATE PUBLIC.
  PUBLIC SECTION.
    METHODS divide_numbers
      IMPORTING
        iv_numerator   TYPE i
        iv_denominator TYPE i
      RETURNING
        VALUE(rv_result) TYPE i
      RAISING
        cx_sy_arithmetic_error.

    METHODS safe_divide
      IMPORTING
        iv_numerator   TYPE i
        iv_denominator TYPE i
      RETURNING
        VALUE(rv_result) TYPE i.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_error_handling IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD divide_numbers.
    IF iv_denominator = 0.
      RAISE EXCEPTION TYPE cx_sy_arithmetic_error
        EXPORTING
          textid = cx_sy_arithmetic_error=>cx_sy_arithmetic_error.
    ENDIF.
    rv_result = iv_numerator / iv_denominator.
  ENDMETHOD.

  METHOD safe_divide.
    TRY.
        rv_result = divide_numbers( iv_numerator = iv_numerator iv_denominator = iv_denominator ).
      CATCH cx_sy_arithmetic_error.
        " Fehlerbehandlung: z.B. Loggen, Standardwert zurückgeben
        rv_result = 0. " Oder ein anderer Fehlerwert
        MESSAGE 'Division durch Null abgefangen, Ergebnis ist 0.' TYPE 'S' DISPLAY LIKE 'E'.
    ENDTRY.
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.
unit_test:
CLASS ltcl_test DEFINITION FOR TESTING RISK LEVEL HARMLESS DURATION SHORT.
  PRIVATE SECTION.
    METHODS test_division_by_zero FOR TESTING RAISING cx_static_check.
    METHODS test_safe_division FOR TESTING.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS ltcl_test IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD test_division_by_zero.
    DATA(lo_cut) = NEW zcl_error_handling( ).
    " Erwartet, dass eine Ausnahme ausgelöst wird
    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_raises( act = `lo_cut->divide_numbers( iv_numerator = 10 iv_denominator = 0 )`
                                        exp_class = 'CX_SY_ARITHMETIC_ERROR' ).
  ENDMETHOD.

  METHOD test_safe_division.
    DATA(lo_cut) = NEW zcl_error_handling( ).
    DATA(lv_result_ok) = lo_cut->safe_divide( iv_numerator = 10 iv_denominator = 2 ).
    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_equals( act = lv_result_ok exp = 5 ).

    DATA(lv_result_error) = lo_cut->safe_divide( iv_numerator = 10 iv_denominator = 0 ).
    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_equals( act = lv_result_error exp = 0 ).
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.
explanation: Die `TRY...CATCH` Blöcke sind der moderne Standard für die Fehlerbehandlung in ABAP. Sie ermöglichen es, Ausnahmen (Exceptions) gezielt abzufangen und darauf zu reagieren, anstatt Programmabbrüche zu riskieren. Die Verwendung von vordefinierten Ausnahmeklassen wie `cx_sy_arithmetic_error` sorgt für eine robuste und standardisierte Fehlerbehandlung.
keywords: Error Handling, TRY CATCH, Exception, CX_SY_ARITHMETIC_ERROR, ABAP 7.50

Instructions: Berechne die Gesamtzahl der belegten Sitze aller Flüge des Carriers 'LH' aus der Tabelle `SFLIGHT`.

solution:
CLASS zcl_reduce_demo DEFINITION PUBLIC FINAL CREATE PUBLIC.
  PUBLIC SECTION.
    METHODS get_total_seats_lh
      RETURNING
        VALUE(rv_total_seats) TYPE i.

CLASS zcl_reduce_demo IMPLEMENTATION.

    DATA lt_sflight TYPE STANDARD TABLE OF sflight.
    SELECT * FROM sflight INTO TABLE @lt_sflight.

explanation: Der `COND` Ausdruck ermöglicht eine kompakte und direkte Zuweisung eines Wertes basierend auf einer Bedingung. Dies ist eine moderne Alternative zu `IF...ENDIF` für einfache bedingte Logik und verbessert die Lesbarkeit.
keywords: COND_EXPRESSION, CONDITIONAL_LOGIC, EXPRESSIONS

Instructions: Definiere eine Konstante für die maximale Anzahl von Flügen pro Tag in einer Klasse und greife darauf zu.
hint: Deklariere die Konstante im `PUBLIC SECTION` der Klasse.
solution:
CLASS zcl_constants_demo DEFINITION PUBLIC FINAL CREATE PUBLIC.
  PUBLIC SECTION.
    CONSTANTS: gc_max_flights_per_day TYPE i VALUE 100.

    METHODS get_max_flights
      RETURNING
        VALUE(rv_max_flights) TYPE i.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_constants_demo IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD get_max_flights.
    rv_max_flights = gc_max_flights_per_day.
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.
unit_test:
CLASS ltcl_test DEFINITION FOR TESTING RISK LEVEL HARMLESS DURATION SHORT.
  PRIVATE SECTION.
    METHODS test_get_max_flights FOR TESTING.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS ltcl_test IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD test_get_max_flights.
    DATA(lo_cut) = NEW zcl_constants_demo( ).
    DATA(lv_max_flights) = lo_cut->get_max_flights( ).

    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_equals(
      act = lv_max_flights,
      exp = 100,
      msg = 'Konstante sollte den Wert 100 haben.'
    ).

    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_equals(
      act = zcl_constants_demo=>gc_max_flights_per_day,
      exp = 100,
      msg = 'Direkter Zugriff auf Konstante sollte funktionieren.'
    ).
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.
explanation: Die Deklaration von Konstanten innerhalb einer Klasse (`CONSTANTS`) ist eine bewährte Praxis in der objektorientierten Programmierung. Es verbessert die Kapselung und Lesbarkeit, da die Konstante direkt mit der Klasse assoziiert ist und über den Klassennamen (`zcl_constants_demo=>gc_max_flights_per_day`) zugegriffen werden kann.
keywords: CONSTANTS, CLASS, OBJECT_ORIENTATION, GLOBAL_CONSTANTS

Instructions: Filtere eine interne Tabelle von Flügen nach einer bestimmten Flugnummer (`CONNID`).
hint: Nutze den `FILTER` Operator, um eine neue Tabelle mit den gefilterten Einträgen zu erstellen.
solution:
CLASS zcl_filter_table_demo DEFINITION PUBLIC FINAL CREATE PUBLIC.
  PUBLIC SECTION.
    TYPES tt_sflight TYPE STANDARD TABLE OF sflight WITH EMPTY KEY.

    METHODS get_flights_by_connid
      IMPORTING
        iv_connid TYPE sflight-connid
      RETURNING
        VALUE(rt_filtered_flights) TYPE tt_sflight.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_filter_table_demo IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD get_flights_by_connid.
    DATA lt_all_flights TYPE tt_sflight.
    SELECT * FROM sflight INTO TABLE @lt_all_flights.

    rt_filtered_flights = FILTER #( lt_all_flights WHERE connid = iv_connid ).
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.
unit_test:
CLASS ltcl_test DEFINITION FOR TESTING RISK LEVEL HARMLESS DURATION SHORT.
  PRIVATE SECTION.
    METHODS test_get_flights_by_connid FOR TESTING.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS ltcl_test IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD test_get_flights_by_connid.
    DATA(lo_cut) = NEW zcl_filter_table_demo( ).
    DATA(lv_test_connid) = '0400'.
    DATA(lt_filtered_flights) = lo_cut->get_flights_by_connid( lv_test_connid ).

    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_initial(
      act = lt_filtered_flights,
      msg = 'Tabelle sollte nicht leer sein, wenn Flüge mit CONNID 0400 existieren.',
      level = cl_abap_unit_assert=>severity_info
    ).

    LOOP AT lt_filtered_flights INTO DATA(ls_flight).
      cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_equals(
        act = ls_flight-connid,
        exp = lv_test_connid,
        msg = 'Alle gefilterten Flüge sollten die korrekte Flugnummer haben.'
      ).
    ENDLOOP.
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.
explanation: Der `FILTER` Operator bietet eine elegante und performante Möglichkeit, interne Tabellen basierend auf einer Bedingung zu filtern. Er erstellt eine neue Tabelle mit den passenden Einträgen, ohne die Originaltabelle zu modifizieren, und ist eine moderne Alternative zu `LOOP AT ... WHERE` mit `APPEND`.
keywords: FILTER_OPERATOR, INTERNAL_TABLES, FILTERING

Instructions: Erstelle ein Objekt einer Klasse und rufe mehrere Methoden in einer Kette auf.
hint: Verwende den `NEW` Operator für die Objekterstellung und Methodenketten (`->method1( )->method2( )`).
solution:
CLASS zcl_method_chain_demo DEFINITION PUBLIC FINAL CREATE PUBLIC.
  PUBLIC SECTION.
    DATA mv_value TYPE i READ-ONLY.

    METHODS constructor IMPORTING iv_initial_value TYPE i.
    METHODS add IMPORTING iv_add_value TYPE i RETURNING VALUE(ro_self) TYPE REF TO zcl_method_chain_demo.
    METHODS multiply IMPORTING iv_mult_value TYPE i RETURNING VALUE(ro_self) TYPE REF TO zcl_method_chain_demo.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_method_chain_demo IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD constructor.
    mv_value = iv_initial_value.
  ENDMETHOD.

  METHOD add.
    mv_value = mv_value + iv_add_value.
    ro_self = me.
  ENDMETHOD.

  METHOD multiply.
    mv_value = mv_value * iv_mult_value.
    ro_self = me.
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.
unit_test:
CLASS ltcl_test DEFINITION FOR TESTING RISK LEVEL HARMLESS DURATION SHORT.
  PRIVATE SECTION.
    METHODS test_method_chaining FOR TESTING.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS ltcl_test IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD test_method_chaining.
    DATA(lo_calculator) = NEW zcl_method_chain_demo( iv_initial_value = 5 ).

    lo_calculator->add( 3 )->multiply( 2 ).

    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_equals(
      act = lo_calculator->mv_value,
      exp = 16, " (5 + 3) * 2 = 16
      msg = 'Method Chaining sollte korrekt funktionieren.'
    ).
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.
explanation: Method Chaining ermöglicht es, mehrere Methodenaufrufe auf demselben Objekt in einer einzigen Anweisung zu verketten. Dies verbessert die Lesbarkeit und den Fluss des Codes, insbesondere bei Fluent Interfaces. Jede Methode, die verkettet werden soll, muss eine Referenz auf das eigene Objekt (`me`) zurückgeben.
keywords: METHOD_CHAINING, NEW_OPERATOR, OBJECT_ORIENTATION, FLUENT_INTERFACE

Instructions: Lese dynamisch den Wert eines Feldes aus einer Struktur, dessen Name zur Laufzeit bekannt ist.
hint: Verwende `ASSIGN COMPONENT` mit `FIELD-SYMBOLS` oder den `GET REFERENCE` Operator.
solution:
CLASS zcl_dynamic_field_access DEFINITION PUBLIC FINAL CREATE PUBLIC.
  PUBLIC SECTION.
    TYPES: BEGIN OF ty_data,
             field1 TYPE string,
             field2 TYPE i,
           END OF ty_data.

    METHODS get_field_value_dynamic
      IMPORTING
        is_data     TYPE ty_data
        iv_field_name TYPE string
      RETURNING
        VALUE(rv_field_value) TYPE string.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS zcl_dynamic_field_access IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD get_field_value_dynamic.
    FIELD-SYMBOLS <lv_field> TYPE any.

    ASSIGN COMPONENT iv_field_name OF STRUCTURE is_data TO <lv_field>.

    IF sy-subrc = 0.
      rv_field_value = <lv_field>.
    ELSE.
      rv_field_value = 'Feld nicht gefunden'.
    ENDIF.
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.
unit_test:
CLASS ltcl_test DEFINITION FOR TESTING RISK LEVEL HARMLESS DURATION SHORT.
  PRIVATE SECTION.
    METHODS test_get_field_value_dynamic FOR TESTING.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS ltcl_test IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD test_get_field_value_dynamic.
    DATA(lo_cut) = NEW zcl_dynamic_field_access( ).
    DATA(ls_test_data) = VALUE zcl_dynamic_field_access=>ty_data( field1 = 'Testwert' field2 = 123 ).

    DATA(lv_value1) = lo_cut->get_field_value_dynamic( is_data = ls_test_data iv_field_name = 'FIELD1' ).
    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_equals(
      act = lv_value1,
      exp = 'Testwert',
      msg = 'Wert von FIELD1 sollte korrekt gelesen werden.'
    ).

    DATA(lv_value2) = lo_cut->get_field_value_dynamic( is_data = ls_test_data iv_field_name = 'FIELD2' ).
    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_equals(
      act = lv_value2,
      exp = '123',
      msg = 'Wert von FIELD2 sollte korrekt gelesen werden.'
    ).

    DATA(lv_value_invalid) = lo_cut->get_field_value_dynamic( is_data = ls_test_data iv_field_name = 'INVALID_FIELD' ).
    cl_abap_unit_assert=>assert_equals(
      act = lv_value_invalid,
      exp = 'Feld nicht gefunden',
      msg = 'Fehlermeldung für ungültiges Feld.'
    ).
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.
explanation: Der dynamische Zugriff auf Felder einer Struktur zur Laufzeit ist ein fortgeschrittenes Feature. `ASSIGN COMPONENT ... TO FIELD-SYMBOL` ist die klassische und immer noch gültige Methode. Alternativ kann `GET REFERENCE` verwendet werden, um eine Datenreferenz auf das Feld zu erhalten. Dies ist nützlich für generische Verarbeitungsroutinen.
keywords: DYNAMIC_PROGRAMMING, FIELD_SYMBOLS, ASSIGN_COMPONENT, RTTI
